name: Achalpur

queries.query: Achalpur Maharashtra official cadastral parcel map land records GIS official
queries.result: First-party discovery found the official Amravati district page for the Deputy Superintendent Land Records Office, Achalpur, the Maharashtra Bhumi Abhilekh services page, and the Mahabhumi dashboard. The official services describe e-Maps/Bhu Naksha and survey-number maps, but discovery did not expose an anonymous parcel API response.

queries.result: Native-language first-party discovery found Maharashtra Bhumi Abhilekh pages describing भू-नकाशा/e-नकाशा, village maps, and survey-number maps. The pages identify the state land-record custodian and the Achalpur office, but no bounded anonymous parcel ID-plus-geometry response was exposed.

registryEvidence: The official Amravati district administration page names a Deputy Superintendent Land Records Office for Achalpur. Maharashtra Bhumi Abhilekh/Mahabhumi is the state first-party land-record custodian and documents Bhu Naksha/e-Maps and survey-number maps. This evidences a local registry/cadastre custodian and public service lead, not an open parcel feature response.

officialSources.observation: Official District Amravati document page titled Deputy Superintendent Land Records Office, Achalpur; it links an office document/PDF. No parcel geometry was present in the HTML page.
Official Maharashtra Bhumi Abhilekh services page lists e-Maps/Bhu Naksha, 7/12, 8A, property-card and e-record services.
Official Mahabhumi dashboard identifies Mahabhunakasha (maps with land records) and state-authorized digital land-record services.

source: District Amravati Deputy Superintendent Land Records Office, Achalpur; Maharashtra Bhumi Abhilekh/Mahabhumi Bhu Naksha lead

requestOutcomes.outcome: TLS-default curl succeeded; the page identified the official Achalpur land-records office and linked an office PDF. No parcel schema or geometry response was present.

First-party discovery returned the official service page and documented e-Maps/Bhu Naksha and survey-number map services. A direct TLS-default curl attempt timed out after 25 seconds before a response body was received.
First-party discovery returned the official dashboard and Mahabhunakasha lead. No anonymous feature schema or geometry response was exposed; no login or credential flow was attempted.

First-party indexed service page showed district, taluka/office, village/city and survey-number inputs for 7/12 lookup. This is a record lookup UI, not evidence of an open parcel geometry API; no unsafe fields were requested.

First-party discovery identified an official MRSAC Taluka Achalpur village-map PDF sourced from Maharashtra Land Record Department maps. It is a village-boundary overview, not a parcel feature service, so no parcel sample was retained.
